RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Thursday,  the October 23, 2008/Kartika 1, 1930 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Prime Minister; Atomic Energy; Coal; Communications and
Information Technology; Development of North Eastern Region;
Environment and Forests; External Affairs; Housing and Urban
Poverty Alleviation; Overseas Indian Affairs; Panchayati Raj;
Parliamentary Affairs; Personnel, Public Grievances and
Pensions; Planning; Shipping, Road Transport and
Highways; Space; Statistics and Programme
Implementation; Urban Development;
Y outh Affairs and Sports)
Total number of questions — 20
28
Hotel accommodation for
Commonwealth Games
*81. SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL:
Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a)  the exact position regarding
availability of approved rooms in both star
and budget category hotels in Delhi as
against reported demand of 50,000
approved rooms, keeping in view the 2010
Commonwealth Games;
(b)  whether DDA has sent any
proposal to his Ministry to increase the
Floor Area Ratio (FAR) of all existing as
well as upcoming hotels in the city;
(c)  if so, whether DDA's proposal has
been approved; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Sharing of information on terror cases
*82. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
 Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether India and Pakistan have
decided to share information on terror cases;
(b)  if so, whether he, recently had a
telephonic conversation with his Pakistani
counterpart to seek revival of the bilateral
dialogue;
(c)  whether during his visit, both
Governments have agreed to fight terror
together;
(d)  if so, whether any agreement in this
regard has been worked out;
(e)  if so, the details thereof; and
(f) to what extent both the countries
have drawn up a plan of  joint action against
terrorism?

29
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Untapped reserves of uranium in
India
*83. SHRIMATI JAYA BACHCHAN:
SHRI N.K. SINGH:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a)  whether it is a fact that our neclear
plants are presently starved because of non-
availability of uranium;
(b)  if so, whether it is a fact that there
are massive untapped reserves of uranium,
estimated at over 1 lakh tonnes, in the States
of Jharkhand, Meghalaya, Andhra Pradesh,
Rajasthan and Tamil Nadu; and
(c)  the reasons for these reserves having
remained untapped, whereas we have been
pursuing foreign resources?
Traffic condition in cities
†*84. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a)  whether it is a fact that traffic
condition has become difficult not only in
big cities but also in small cities due to
increasing  production of buses, scooters,
motorcycles and cars and the usage thereof;
(b)  if so, the reaction of Government in
this regard;
(c)  whether Government would
formulate any national level action plan to
resolve this problem;
(d)  if so, the details thereof; and
(e)  if not,the reasons for not including
it under the Jawaharlal Nehru National
Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) for a
solution?
Schemes to promote sports
*85.  SHRI KUMAR DEEPAK DAS:
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS
AND SPORTS be pleased to state:
(a)  whether Government is aware that
most of the Panchayat areas in the country
are lacking in sports infrastructure;
(b)  if so, whether Government would
consider some specific sports
encouragement scheme at every panchayat
level;
(c)  whether Government would adopt
any specific policy to promote sports at
grass root level; and
(d)  whether Government would
consider to reserve at least 5 per cent
employment for the sportspersons in
Central and State Government and
corporate sector?
LCD production in the country
*86. SHRI PRAKASH JA V ADEKAR:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMA TION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a)  whether it is a fact that Government
has decided to encourage Liquid Crystal
Display (LCD) production in the country;
(b)  if so, the details of concessions
offered and its policy, if any; and
(c)  whether Government has instructed
State Governments to offer similar
concessions?

30
Challenges of climate change
*87. SHRI  JESUDASU SEELAM:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a)  whether India, with a coastline of
about 7,500 kms. risks losing a significant
number of lives and assets worth $3.85
trillion due to coastal flooding that may
occur as a result of climate change in 2070,
as per global study conducted by the
Organisation for Economic Cooperation
Development;
(b)  whether the report notes that those
cities with greatest population exposure to
extreme sea levels also tend to be those
with greatest exposure to wind damage from
tropical and extra tropical cyclones; and
(c)  if so, the concrete steps and measures
Government  proposes to take to meet the
challenge of climatic change?
Chines
